correctness.rationale: Every valid linear superstring induces an ordered Hamiltonian path through the 32 required equal-length squares, and maximal suffix-prefix overlap concatenation realizes every path cost. The eight length-five root necklaces force q>=7 cross transitions and L>=41+5q; q>=9 costs at least 86. The exact 8-class subset DP yields minimum 82 for q=7. The only q=8 possibility at length <=81 requires all cost-one internal transitions and cost-six cross transitions; those force one primitive 5-cycle split, and an exhaustive 120-case nine-block DP finds no feasible equality path. A literal 82-bit witness contains all 32 squares, verified by direct factor enumeration. The standard-library proof verifier and the separately formulated integer-programming check both executed successfully.

value.rationale: The sharpness of the length-82 greedy cover resolves a concrete unresolved point of the natural all-squares superstring problem treated in Au 2009/2015. The certified gap from the published general lower bound 72 to the exact optimum 82 is nontrivial and comes from the intrinsic topology of the six five-root necklace cycles. Exact finite optimality at the first 32-square instance, with a reusable crossing obstruction, is mathematically motivated without claiming an all-length theorem.
